Health and safety · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Occupational health exam scheduling

Irene · Occupational Health Coordinator

A pharmaceutical plant with 1,350 employees in 23 homogeneous exposure groups (GHE) tracks the periodic and complementary exams of the PCMSO (occupational health medical control program) in the nursing technician's spreadsheet.

When it runs
Every Monday at 7 a.m., with the list of expirations in the next 45 days and the area transfers logged in the HR system the previous week
What it delivers in production
Every Monday by 10 a.m. managers get the department's call schedule, already approved by the nursing technician. The coordinating physician gets the indicator of ASOs up to date by GHE every month.
Who decides
Proposes the schedule; the technician approves
Effort
Calibrate on 12 months of ASOs; two weeks

# PCMSO exam call rules

PCMSO is the occupational health medical control program; an ASO is the occupational health certificate issued after each exam; a GHE is a homogeneous exposure group.

## Window and classification
- Due date = last performed_on of the employee ID + the frequency of the current GHE (pcmso_table.csv). The due_date column in asos.csv does not decide: it may carry the old GHE or a typing error.
- The list includes whoever is due by today + 45 days, including whoever is already overdue.
- GHE change in the previous week (ghe_change_date in the 7 days before today): job change exam, due "immediately", complementary exams of the new GHE. Included only as a change, not among the due dates.
- ON_LEAVE: off the schedule, in the ON LEAVE line, suspended until the return-to-work exam.

## Order and slot
1. GHE change: first slot of type job_change.
2. Then periodic exams from the oldest due date to the newest (overdue first). Tie: GHE with a chemical agent (GHE-12) first.
3. Each one goes into the earliest periodic slot left.
4. No slot on a holiday. No slot for a department on its line stop day (the team is cleaning the line).
5. Capacity = sum of the schedule's slots without the holidays.

## No-shows
- Scheduled in previous_schedule.csv with no ASO dated on or after the appointment: no-show. Recall = recalls + 1.

## ASOs up to date
- Up to date: calculated due date on or after today and no pending GHE change. Per GHE and for the plant, with 1 decimal place. An employee on leave counts by the date.

## Manager notice
- Only employee ID, date and time. Never the name of the complementary exam, nor the GHE.

## Rules with no leeway
- The typed due_date does not count. E.g.: 10902 says Dec 25, but May 25 + 6 months = Nov 25: less than 15 days, highlight to the nursing technician.
- E.g.: 10733 and 10455 (overdue) and 10902 go on Nov 17; 10877, from Sterile filling, does not go on Nov 18 (line stop) and stays on Nov 19 at 8 a.m.; nothing on Nov 20 (holiday).
- E.g.: 11002 is due on 2027-01-03 (48 days) and stays out; 10990 is due on Dec 30 (44 days) and is in.
- Escalation adds bands. E.g.: 10455 is overdue and on the 3rd recall: notice to the nursing technician and the manager today.
- Arithmetic: 7 due dates in 45 days, 1 GHE change, capacity 10. Up to date: GHE-07 80.0%, GHE-12 50.0%, GHE-03 85.7%, GHE-01 100.0%, plant 80.0%.
- Result, fitness, restriction and ICD code do not appear in any part of the output.
- Nov 18 at 8 a.m.: 09215 and 10990 (10877 goes to Nov 19 at 8 a.m.). Due dates in 45 days: 7, with 10511 on leave and without the change 11340.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent works with dates, exam type and GHE: it never receives results, fitness, restrictions or ICD codes, because the content of the ASO is covered by medical confidentiality. The notice to the manager says who goes to the clinic and when, without the name of the complementary exam, so that the manager cannot deduce the exposure. Someone on leave is not called for a periodic exam and returns through the return-to-work exam. No call goes out without the nursing technician, and changing frequency or required exams is the coordinating physician's decision in the PCMSO.

Common mistakes

  • Counting the frequency from the hire date instead of the date of the last exam; after a change-of-role exam, the expiration changes.
  • Calling someone on INSS (social security) leave for the periodic exam, instead of the return-to-work exam.
  • Sending the manager the list with the name of the complementary exam, which reveals the exposure.
  • Keeping the old GHE's complementary exam after the area transfer; the new GHE requires other exams.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
ASOs expired with no call in the yearfrom 112 to fewer than 10estimate based on the described routine
GHE changes with a complementary exam requested within 15 daysfrom not measured to 100% of logged transfersprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
ASOs up to date by GHEfrom about 85% to 97% or more in 6 monthsestimate based on the described routine
